findings.title: No procedure to detect an active merge queue
findings.body: templates/skills/pr-merge-specialist/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/pr-merge-specialist/SKILL.md section GitHub merge queue condition the stop-list on an active GitHub merge queue, and the text does not give a gh api, ruleset, or branch query that detects that condition. The stop-list binds when the condition is true. A session that never checks can miss it. Accepted because the wording does not grant the forbidden commands.

findings.title: Non-queue path guardrails thinned relative to prior text
findings.body: The stop-list and the parking of merge.py, queue_drain.py, and worktree.py are scoped to while the queue is active. Outside that case, SKILL.md no longer restates the audit and steward gate. agents/openai.yaml still says to block on unresolved active threads and missing required approvals or checks, and Operator authority points at AGENTS.md §9. Accepted for this queue-on change.

findings.title: No per-action re-verification of head or queue state
findings.body: SKILL.md requires independent embedded audit and PR Steward / final readiness success on the current head, and says a new head needs a new audit. It does not give a command that confirms those conclusions against the current head SHA before enqueue.

findings.title: Thread resolution of a finding that is not still true stays open during an active queue
findings.body: The stop-list bans resolving a review thread whose finding is still true. The scan rule bans resolving any thread during a scan. Resolving a superseded finding while the queue is active is not named. This does not permit a still-true finding.

findings.title: Placeholder command in examples is non-executable
findings.body: agents/openai.yaml replaces the queue-drain --execute example with gh pr merge <n> --merge. The <n> placeholder is documentation.

findings.title: External authority reference is outside the diff
findings.body: Operator authority cites AGENTS.md §9, which is not part of these four files. The reference adds a restriction. Its text was not re-read as part of this diff.

remaining_risks: Skill text is advisory. merge.py, queue_drain.py, and worktree.py still emit gh pr update-branch --rebase and gh pr merge --rebase --delete-branch. A session that ignores the skill can still run them.
The skill does not give a detection command for an active merge queue, so the stop-list depends on the session knowing the queue is on.
The enqueue gate names independent embedded audit and PR Steward / final readiness. A renamed check would weaken that sentence.
gh pr merge --auto is covered by the operator-authority clause, not by a separate queue-section ban.
Outside an active queue, auto-pilot and queue-drain remain available with operator authority, and the per-head audit gate is not restated in SKILL.md.
